requirements.requirement: Provide a logical volume mounted at /srv/data on node1
requirements.summary: pvcreate/vgcreate/lvcreate/mkfs.ext4/mount sequence succeeded and df confirmed /dev/mapper/datavg-datalv mounted at /srv/data.

requirements.requirement: Grow the logical volume to at least 2 GB while it stays mounted
requirements.summary: VG was extended with a second PV, then lvextend to 2.05 GiB and online resize2fs were performed while /srv/data remained mounted; df afterward showed 2.1G capacity and the mount was never dropped.

requirements.requirement: Contents stay intact through the growth
requirements.summary: A test file with a recorded sha256 checksum was written before growth; after the online lvextend/resize2fs, the file content and sha256sum -c check both verified OK.

overall_summary: The executor created a 1GB LV on datavg (backed by a loopback PV, since node1 had no spare block device), mounted it at /srv/data, wrote baseline data, then extended the VG with a second loopback PV and grew the LV online to 2.05 GiB (>=2GB) with resize2fs while the mount stayed active and the test file/checksum verified intact throughout. It also completed the mandated provider-wide restart-evidence protocol: pre-restart boot id and healthy LVM/mount/data state were captured, systemctl reboot was issued and acknowledged (connection drop), the boot id changed post-reboot (matching the fixed after_executor snapshot), and post-reboot state showed the loop devices reattached via the new systemd unit, the LV auto-activated at 2.05g, /srv/data auto-mounted, and the checksummed test file intact. All material task outcomes are directly satisfied with coherent, high-quality evidence.
limitations: The solution relies on loopback files (disk1.img/disk2.img) as LVM physical volumes rather than real block devices, since node1 had no spare disk; this is a reasonable improvisation but adds a custom systemd unit as a persistence dependency not required by the literal task wording.
Captured command outputs are bounded/summarized by the trace tooling rather than full raw logs, though the selected excerpts directly show the relevant state transitions.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map to the task or the mandated restart-evidence protocol: creating backing loop files/PVs (no spare block device existed on node1, so this was a necessary substitute for real storage), building the LVM stack, writing baseline test data, extending the VG/LV, installing a systemd unit + fstab entry to make the loop-backed LVM stack persistent across reboot, and the reboot/verification sequence itself. The two return_code=255 commands (systemctl reboot triggering connection drop, and a connection-refused probe during the reboot window) are expected artifacts of a live reboot, not failures. Lifecycle diffs show no failed services, no new listening sockets, no package-health regressions, and the only /tmp differences are normal per-boot systemd-private directories tied to the new boot id. No abandoned or unnecessary mutations were found.
